conflicts_flagged: Konflikt 6: MindStudio post claims cache 'affect Claude subscription limits (eat rate limit)'. Oficjalne docs not explicit. Resolution: cache read/write tokens counted as usage for rate limits (full tokens, not 10%). GitHub Issue #24147 confirmed.
Konflikt 7: Du'An 2024 post used Sonnet 3.5 pricing. April 2026 Sonnet 4.6 has identical $3/$15 rates - Du'An numbers still applicable but model changed.
Konflikt 11: Spring AI docs (Oct 2025) provide different minimums than official docs (April 2026). Official docs canonical source. Haiku 4.5 = 4096 (not 2048).
Konflikt 12: Community post Aug 2024 launch claimed 'cache only 5 minutes'. Docs since Q4 2024 offer 1h TTL. Old posts may mislead.
Konflikt 13: HN poster claimed write costs '1.2x' not '1.25x'. Official docs exact: 1.25x (5/4). Rounding error.
gaps_flagged: Gap 8: No empirical case studies for Haiku 4.5. Most cases are Sonnet/Opus. Unclear if Haiku patterns identical (likely per ratios, unverified).
Gap 9: No case studies with Batch + Cache stack. Theoretical 95% discount exists, no public benchmark with actual USD numbers.
Gap 10: Fast Mode + Cache interaction unproven. Worth benchmarking (Opus 4.6 only feature).
Gap 11: Haiku 4.5 minimum threshold 4,096 tokens - no developer awareness data. Silent fail pattern may be widespread.
Gap 12: Automatic caching (Feb 2026 API) - no empirical hit rate comparison vs manual breakpoints.
Gap 13: Workspace isolation cost impact - no case studies showing real cost for multi-workspace orgs.
summary: 30 claims extracted. 25 consensus/high-confidence (pricing tables, break-even math, published case studies). 2 disputed (TTL regression severity). 3 low-confidence gaps (Haiku 4.5, Batch+Cache, Fast Mode). 15 claims contain USD or multiplier figures. Conflicts mostly source-version issues (Spring AI Oct 2025 vs official April 2026 docs). Key numbers: Du'An 90% ($648/mo), ProjectDiscovery 70% savings, Spring 68%, Finout 85% ($3,834/mo). Break-even validated: 5m after 1 hit, 1h after 2 hits.
